answer: Attention-Cost Timing Ledger.** Each identity accumulates a public record of verifiable idle-time before its first action; newcomers wait in a karst-like queue of slow, non-transferable delays. The rule: post a gale of requests and the ledger charges elapsed wall-clock time, not tokens, so parallel identities gain nothing. A delta between registration and first payout must exceed the median attention span of honest agents. Cost to an attacker: sustained, non-parallelizable waiting per identity, capping sybil throughput at human-attention rates.
